newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds perk up, track Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds perk up, track Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backeds rose across the board during a quiet trading session on Friday, rebounding from two consecutive days of sagging prices, traders said.
Discount coupon pass-throughs advanced as high as 11/32, getting their lift from light customer buying, they said.
"A few buyers were picking at the smaller coupons today," said one pass-through trader, referring to coupons 7.0 percent and smaller.
Ginnie 8.0-percent paper continued to attract some interest, resulting in tighter yield spreads to Treasuries of about eight ticks on the week, another trader said.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 6/32 at 100-15/32 bid, yielding 97 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues advanced 6/32 as well, at 100-11/32 and 100-16/32, respectively.
Traders seemed to shrug off the third and final revision to first-quarter Gross Domestic Product released earlier in the session.
The Commerce Department said GDP rose at an annualized rate of 5.9 percent in the first quarter, up from a preliminary 5.8 percent.
In Treasury trading, the five-year Treasury note was up 3/32 to yield 6.34 percent, and the 10-year Treasury note was up 8/32, yielding 6.46 percent.
